### Start the OpenAI blockquote where TechCrunch starts it

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-15-carry-1.md`.

The blockquote rendered as OpenAI's words opens "We and the larger AI community do not yet have a clear standard...". I fetched the declared anchor and searched its bytes: "We and the larger AI community do not yet have a clear standard" is MISSING; what the page carries is TechCrunch's own bridge — OpenAI's statement "stating that both OpenAI and 'the larger AI community do not yet have a clear standard for how to report misalignment that shows up during training, evaluation, and deployment, including examples that don't look like traditional security incidents but could provide insight into AI behavior and future risks.'" Everything from "the larger" onward is verbatim; the two words "We and" are the post's own reconstruction of a pronoun TechCrunch elided. The meaning is identical and the primary (the X post) is unreachable, so this is not a wrong claim — but the post's own sourcing block says "Every OpenAI quotation above is TechCrunch's rendering of that post", and for two words it is not. Fix: open the blockquote at "the larger AI community" and lead in with TechCrunch's own framing ("OpenAI's statement said that both it and...").

### Anchor the five weeks of cleanup to the main burst, not to the July bursts

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-15-carry-2.md`.

The post reads "...smaller bursts on 1 and 2 July. Leitner went on deleting agent pages for five weeks after that." WinBuzzer, the cited source, says he "continued removing agent-created pages for five weeks after the main burst ended" — and the main burst ended after 22 June, not after 2 July. As written, "after that" attaches the five weeks to the July bursts and moves the end of the cleanup about ten days later than the source puts it. Fix: "for five weeks after the main burst ended."

2 findings carried by reviewers against `content/wiki/org/bytedance-seed.md`, batched into one job because they concern the same file. Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Declare byteplus.com in publishes_from once the field exists

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-01-carry-1.md`.

The brief required `publishes_from`; it cannot be declared today. `entrySchema` in `lib/schema.mjs` is `.strict()` and rejects the key — measured: `entrySchema.safeParse({...entry, publishes_from: ['bytedance.com']})` returns `Unrecognized key: "publishes_from"` — and `grep publishes_from lib/` returns no matches, because the field lives only in the pending `separate-a-claim-from-a-fact` amendment. The live substitute already covers part of the ground: `orgNameTokens` in `lib/render/frontier.mjs` derives the token `bytedance` from this entry's display name, so a claim cited from `seed.bytedance.com` attributes correctly with no declaration. What it does not cover is the domain this entry itself establishes as the only place the model can be called from abroad — `ai.byteplus.com`, whose registrable label `byteplus` is not one of the org's name tokens. When the field lands, this entry needs `publishes_from: [byteplus.com]`, or a real BytePlus-hosted Seed claim renders as the honest-looking blank FM-N6 describes.

### Reconsider the bare "Seed" alias — it widens two joins that ignore alias class

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-01-carry-2.md`.

The entry declares `- name: Seed / class: manual`. `manual` correctly keeps the linker off it, but neither mechanism that reads this list looks at `class`: `matchProviders` and `orgNameTokens` in `lib/render/frontier.mjs` both map `aliases[].name` with a 3-character floor and nothing else. So `seed` becomes (a) a board-join key that matches any future catalog provider id containing the substring — today only `bytedance-seed`, tomorrow anything a router files under a name with `seed` in it — and (b) an ownership token, making any registrable domain whose bought label is exactly `seed` read as this organisation's own. The alias buys nothing in return, since `manual` means it is never wrapped in prose. Dropping it, or narrowing it to a form that carries the vendor name, would close both without any loss.

Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Cite the three comparison likes counts, or narrow the fact to the one the URL supports

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-03-carry-1.md`.

The fact `hermes_4_likes` carries "299, against 215 for Hermes-4-70B, 181 for Hermes-4-14B and 94 for Hermes-4-405B" with a single `source_url`, https://huggingface.co/api/models/NousResearch/Hermes-4.3-36B. That document contains only the 299. I fetched all four endpoints on 2026-09-06 and every number is right (Hermes-4.3-36B likes=299, Hermes-4-70B likes=215, Hermes-4-14B likes=181, Hermes-4-405B likes=94), so nothing is false — but a reader following the rendered link can check one figure in four, and the wiki spec requires a fact's source be reachable from the rendered page. Either split the comparison into per-model facts each citing its own `/api/models/...` endpoint, or reduce this fact to the 299 and move the comparison into prose that names the other three URLs.

### The portal row count does not reproduce at 332

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260906-03-carry-2.md`.

`portal_catalog` states "332 distinct named model rows, counted from the landing page's own per-1M price cells". Fetching https://portal.nousresearch.com/ on 2026-09-06 (the fact's own `accessed` date) and extracting the embedded `{"displayName","modelName","tokenPrice"}` rows gives 346 rows, 346 distinct `modelName`, 337 distinct `displayName`, and 333 distinct `modelName` once the 13 `~`-prefixed free-tier duplicate ids are dropped. No counting convention I tried lands on 332; the nearest is 333. Same-day drift of one row is the likely explanation and this is not blocking, but the figure should either be re-counted with the convention stated ("distinct model ids, free-tier duplicates excluded") or softened. The load-bearing half of the claim is exactly right and I confirmed it: of all 346 rows, zero match /nous|hermes|nomos|consilience|psyche/ in either id or display name.

### Two launch-post quotes are classed `slow` where `dated` is what they are

Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Fix the GitSpawn disclosure date before the post is written — Manifold's page carries Sep 1, not Sep 2

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260905-05-carry-1.md`.

The candidate's summary says "the vulnerability class Manifold Security disclosed on 2026-09-02" and its why-now says the agents were "still unpatched at disclosure three days ago". Fetching https://www.manifold.security/blog/ai-coding-agents-git-hijack on 2026-09-05 returns a byline date of "Sep 1, 2026", and an independent search corroborates it — "On Monday, Sep 1, 2026, Manifold Security published a research post by Francisco Rosales that names a class called GitSpawn", with "four of the eight flaws remained unpatched as of September 1". 2026-09-02 is The Hacker News's publication date, not the disclosure date — the docket's own evidence block correctly dates the THN piece 2026-09-02, so the two look to have been merged. Fix: the authoring job should read the Manifold page's raw HTML, take the disclosure date from it, and keep the THN date attached to THN. The why-now's "still unpatched at disclosure three days ago" needs the same correction.

### "Eight agents were reported affected" is eight findings across seven agents

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260905-05-carry-2.md`.

The GitSpawn candidate's summary says "Eight agents were reported affected" and then lists seven products (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI and Desktop, Cursor, goose, Hermes Agent, Qwen Code, Grok Build). Manifold's table does have eight rows, but Claude Code occupies two of them — the core.fsmonitor path (patched 2.1.196) and the ultrareview path (unpatched at 2.1.252). Independent coverage counts it the same way — "GitSpawn, Seven Coding Agents", and "four of the eight flaws remained unpatched as of September 1". Fix: the post should say eight findings across seven agents, which also makes the "four fixed, four unpatched" split parse correctly.

### The docket's account of what The Hacker News says about CVE-2026-71963 may itself be wrong

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260905-05-carry-3.md`.

The candidate flags a discrepancy: "the Manifold table as extracted attributes CVE-2026-71963 to Hermes Agent; The Hacker News attributes CVE-2026-71963 to Grok Build". Fetching the THN piece on 2026-09-05 returns "VulnCheck assigned CVE-2026-71963, according to Manifold" in the Hermes Agent passage, not the Grok Build one — i.e. the two sources may agree, and the disagreement may be an artifact of the extractor. This changes nothing about the required action, since the docket already instructs the authoring job to check each CVE against MITRE/NVD directly, but the post should not assert that the two outlets disagree without re-reading both in raw HTML first.

The proposal says of `MATERIAL_KINDS`: "`price`, `context` and `status` are material **field** names — they travel on a line's `field`". Parsing all 182 lines, the `field` values actually carried are `price_input` (8), `price_output` (8), `status` (6) and `context_window` (1). Only `status` travels verbatim; `price` and `context` are the spec's and registry's names for the material-field *categories* (`data/sources/registry.json` declares `price_input`, `price_output`, `context_window`). The load-bearing half of the sentence is exactly right and I confirmed it — all three appear as a `kind` on zero of the 182 lines — so this is a dropped qualifier, not a wrong claim. "are the material field categories, carried on a line's `field` as `price_input`, `price_output` and `context_window`" would fix it.

### Name the directive, not the review, as what accepted the publishes_from divergence

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260905-22-carry-2.md`.

`proposal.md`'s new section says SPECREV-001 "answered all seven items above in its 'AUTHOR'S QUESTIONS' section: item 1 stands as drafted". SPECREV-001 declined to decide item 1 — D1 ends "**KEEPER-CLASS** — not decided here" and its Q1 answer is "D1, **KEEPER-CLASS**: the record does say 'aliases' and the author's three mechanical reasons are all real." What accepted the field choice was the directive ("that judgment is ACCEPTED as the better mechanism"), not the review. The requirement text itself is fine; this is one clause of narrative, and the fix is to say the review left item 1 keeper-class and the directive resolved it. Worth correcting because D1's whole purpose is that a divergence read as a decision by a named decider rather than as compliance.

items.detail:
2 findings carried by reviewers against `openspec/changes/separate-a-claim-from-a-fact/specs/wiki/spec.md`, batched into one job because they concern the same file. Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Say why RD-005's first branch had to be replaced, not just that it was

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260905-18-carry-1.md`.

The wiki delta replaces RD-005's own first attribution branch — "one the org entry records citing itself from" (`loops/ui-loop/RULES.md:638-639`) — with a declared `publishes_from`, and states the field "SHALL NOT be inferred from the entry's own cited source URLs", but never says what goes wrong if it is. This tree answers that, and the answer is the change's own motivating defect: all 13 `founded` facts on `content/wiki/org/` cite `en.wikipedia.org` (measured 2026-09-05), so every one of those org entries "records citing itself from" `wikipedia.org` — and RD-005's derived branch, run against this corpus, would attribute a Wikipedia-sourced claim to Anthropic as Anthropic's own words. That is precisely the defect ledger rows 2 and 4 recorded, arriving through the repair. Adding those two sentences to uncertainty item 1 would put the strongest available argument in front of the ui-loop session that is being asked to re-decide `publishes_from` versus `aliases`, where at present the item argues only from `aliases[].name` being classified as a name.

### Say that the restored "records citing itself from" half admits nothing the name-token half does not

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260905-22-carry-3.md`.

As written, the second admission path keeps a cited domain "only where that domain's own registrable label is one of the subject's name tokens", and the third path admits any domain "whose registrable label is one of the subject's name tokens". The first is therefore a strict subset of the second and can never admit a domain alone. This faithfully reproduces the implementation — `orgOwnDomains` keeps a domain on `tokens.has(reg.label)` (`lib/render/frontier.mjs:323`) and `isVendorSourced`'s fallback tests the identical predicate (`lib/render/frontier.mjs:340`) — so it is not a defect introduced here, and `proposal.md` discloses the filter choice. What it does not say is that the filtered half is inert, which is what a later implementer needs: told to build three admission paths, one of them can never fire on its own. One sentence noting it is stated for fidelity with the live rule would close it. The live question underneath — R13 (v)'s prose states the recorded half unfiltered while `frontier.mjs` filters it — is keeper-class and named as such in `proposal.md`.

proposal.md counts "71 lines" as 69 `agentic_index` plus 2 `coding_index` number→absent transitions, and I reproduce those two figures exactly from `previous.json` (2026-09-04T06:00:03.738Z, 427 rows) and `latest.json` (2026-09-05T06:00:04.599Z, 431 rows). But 3 of the 71 are rows that left the snapshot entirely rather than rows that dropped the field: `qwen/qwen3.8-max` (carried both indices) and `ibm-granite/granite-4.1-8b` (carried `coding_index`). Excluding those, 68 surviving rows lost `agentic_index` and **zero** surviving rows lost `coding_index` — a vanished row is handled by the separate last-known-value/repair rule in `specs/wiki`, not by a seeding-signal disappearance. Same instrument shows the "2 gained it" on `coding_index` are the two new arrivals `openai/gpt-6-astra` and its `:batch` twin, not existing rows regaining a value, so the parenthetical "2 rows lost `coding_index` and 2 gained it — so even the stable row is not stationary" is row churn described as field churn. The conclusion is untouched (68/182 is still two fifths), and the draft already flags that instruments differ; the fix is one clause — "71 number→absent transitions, 3 of them rows that left the snapshot altogether" — in proposal.md's finding 2 and in the matching sentence of `specs/wiki/spec.md`.

The revision replaced the old "four listings in five" with "at least two listings in three", in the proposal ("An axis that leaves at least two listings in three with nothing to say") and in the directory delta ("A required field here would force a wrong answer onto at least two listings in three"). At the lower of the two readings the same sentences state — 23 of 35 — the fraction is 0.6571, and two in three of 35 is 23.33, so the "at least" floor is breached by a third of a listing. It holds at the 26 reading (0.7429). Both exact counts are printed alongside, so nothing is hidden, but the qualifier is doing work it does not quite earn. "roughly two listings in three", or simply "onto 23 of the 35", would be exact under either reading.
